content.jointProblem: Can standardised ML-DSA signing and hybrid classical/post-quantum operation be integrated into KL-HSM firmware within its memory, performance and security constraints, supporting a versioned migration roadmap and a proof of concept within twelve months? The first experiment would port and test ML-DSA on a representative KL-HSM using its production toolchain, measuring correctness, peak RAM, flash, signing latency and timing leakage before selecting an integration architecture.

rationale.text: Nikolić has implemented and benchmarked lattice-based signatures in C on Cortex-M4, providing directly relevant experience for investigating KL-HSM signing performance and memory trade-offs.

sources.quote: We implement the NIST post-quantum signature finalists CRYSTALS-Dilithium (security levels 2 and 3) and Falcon-512 in C
Signing is substantially more expensive for Falcon due to the discrete Gaussian sampler: 14.8 ms versus 3.2 ms for Dilithium-2.

rationale.text: Her HSM research connects algorithm adaptation, implementation security and migration-roadmap work, matching the company's need for both firmware integration and a documented transition plan.

sources.quote: Work packages cover algorithm selection and adaptation, FPGA and secure microcontroller implementation, side-channel and fault-injection evaluation, and a migration roadmap document targeting IEC 62443 compliance.

rationale.text: She has investigated compiler-dependent timing leakage in Dilithium, relevant to validating the security of optimised signing firmware rather than relying on algorithm-level assurances.

sources.quote: We compile a reference Dilithium-2 implementation using GCC 11 and Clang 14 at optimisation levels O0 through O3 and Os on ARM Cortex-M4 and x86-64
Leakage detection using Welch's t-test and TVLA methodology crosses the threshold of |t| = 4.5 in three of eight compiler/architecture combinations.

rationale.text: Her embedded PQC benchmarking work offers a reproducible basis for comparing implementation alternatives and reporting performance trade-offs.

sources.quote: We validate the suite by collecting results for Kyber-512, Dilithium-2, Falcon-512, SPHINCS+-SHA2-128s, and Classic McEliece 348864 across all four targets.
We also provide a discussion of what metrics matter most for different deployment scenarios such as TLS handshake, firmware signing, and device attestation.

rationale.text: She has prior company-facing PQC readiness-assessment experience, supporting an applied migration project rather than a purely theoretical study.

sources.quote: Milica Nikolić collaborated with Informatika d.o.o. (Novi Sad) on a six-month applied research contract in 2022 covering PQC readiness assessment for their smart metering gateway product line.

constraints.text: Integration must fit the actual KL-HSM microcontroller's available flash and RAM and its C firmware environment; a drop-in replacement cannot be assumed.

sources.quote: Our HSM firmware runs on a constrained microcontroller with limited flash and RAM, so a straight drop-in is not possible.
Custom ARM Cortex-M firmware in C for HSM cryptographic operations

constraints.text: The scope must address larger key material, changed signature flows and hybrid operation, and produce a roadmap linking firmware versions to measured performance trade-offs.

sources.quote: we have not touched the firmware architecture to accommodate larger key material or different signature flows.
which firmware version will support post-quantum algorithms, what the performance trade-offs are, and how hybrid classical/post-quantum operation will work during transition.

constraints.text: The plan must be scoped to a documented roadmap and at least one working proof-of-concept integration within twelve months, using the company's limited collaborative engineering capacity.

sources.quote: A good outcome is a documented roadmap and at least one working proof-of-concept integration inside twelve months.
with modest capacity to take on collaborative projects if the scope is well-defined and the output is practically applicable.

constraints.text: Architecture changes must be assessed against the company's PKCS#11 integration and Common Criteria EAL4+ target; the research proof of concept must not be presented as certification.

The project should provide access to real target hardware and measurable deliverables. If an SLE97-based experimental route is considered, the laboratory has only two evaluation kits and additional partner hardware may be needed.

sources.quote: Prefers collaborative arrangements that involve real hardware and measurable deliverables rather than purely theoretical work.
The lab has limited availability of the Infineon SLE97 evaluation kits (two units); industrial partners providing additional hardware would accelerate shared projects.

risks: The Cortex-M4 signature results concern finalist-era Dilithium on an STM32F407, not standardised ML-DSA on KL-HSM. The first experiment must establish correctness, resource use and leakage on the actual target; published measurements are not product forecasts.

The demonstrated hybrid HSM architecture combines ECDH and Kyber using a secure microcontroller plus FPGA. It does not validate hybrid signing or a firmware-only KL-HSM migration; an early end-to-end classical/PQC signing and verification experiment is needed.
Memory optimisation and compiler changes may introduce leakage or undermine security assumptions. Initial timing tests will not establish complete side-channel or fault resistance.

The exact MCU variants, memory headroom, production toolchain, hardware access and downstream verifier capabilities are unknown; any of these could force architectural changes beyond the twelve-month proof-of-concept scope.
Joint-project willingness is open, but Nikolić's current availability, the project budget and committed company engineer time are unknown.
The company described an end-of-2025 certification target, but its present certification status and the impact of a PQC branch on the evaluated configuration are unknown.
questions: Can Nikolić commit to the proposed twelve-month joint project, with what start date, personnel and time allocation? What budget and named engineering support can Kriptolog commit?
Which KL-300 or KL-500 configuration should be the first target, and what are its MCU, RAM/flash headroom, toolchain, RTOS, signing throughput and latency requirements?

Can the team access representative HSMs, firmware source, build/debug tools, the existing ML-DSA prototype and a safe laboratory setup using non-production keys? What confidentiality and IP terms apply?

Does the initial scope cover signing customer firmware, verification of KL-HSM firmware updates, general PKCS#11 signing services, or several of these? Which ML-DSA parameter sets and client verifiers must interoperate?
What precisely should hybrid signing mean for clients: signature packaging, verifier acceptance rules, downgrade prevention, key provisioning, rotation and recovery?
What correctness, resource, performance and leakage criteria will govern the first target-hardware experiment, and what fallback scope is acceptable if firmware-only integration does not fit?

What is the current Common Criteria evaluation status and security target, and which certification, side-channel and fault-injection activities must remain outside or inside this project's acceptance criteria?
Who will approve the versioned migration roadmap, and how will it distinguish experimental support, production readiness and any later certification milestones?
